subject: science
title: Launch and diagnostic: physical and chemical properties

standards.legacy_label: Science and engineering practice foundation - this unit claims no Michigan performance expectation.

essential_question: How do chemists decide what a measurement actually tells them, and how do we work safely with matter at home?
learning_objectives: Observe the anchoring phenomenon, surface initial thinking about physical and chemical properties without penalty, and pose a testable question.
Explain physical and chemical properties using evidence, a model, or a documented process rather than an unsupported answer.
Apply physical and chemical properties to a task the learner has not seen before, showing the reasoning that produced the result.
Check and revise the work on physical and chemical properties against the stated success criteria and name the next step.
success_criteria: The learner completes the central task about physical and chemical properties.
The learner supplies evidence, reasoning, a model, or a documented process, not a bare answer.
The learner checks or revises the work and identifies one specific next step.
Any quantity the learner reports is one the learner measured, computed, or cited to a named published source.
materials: course notebook or digital equivalent
pencil, keyboard, or other accessible response tool
printed or on-screen text, data table, or model for this lesson

lesson_flow.title: Retrieval and phenomenon check
lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action: Open with the unit phenomenon - Two people measure the same spoon of salt and get masses that differ by more than the salt they think they added. - or a short retrieval prompt on physical and chemical properties. Ask the learner to notice, predict, estimate, or question before any instruction. Record the prediction; it is not graded.

lesson_flow.title: Model or mini-lesson
lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action: Develop physical and chemical properties from the phenomenon: pose the testable question, build or use a model, and show how evidence constrains the explanation. Name the success criteria and demonstrate how to check the work. Phase focus: Launch and diagnostic.

lesson_flow.title: Guided practice
lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action: Work two supported examples on physical and chemical properties, asking after each move: what evidence or reasoning supports that step? Fade the prompting on the second example and have the learner narrate the check.

lesson_flow.title: Independent application
lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action: The learner completes a new application of physical and chemical properties independently and records both the result and the reasoning, evidence, process, or design choice that produced it.

lesson_flow.title: Exit evidence and next step
lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action: In one concise response, the learner shows or explains the most important idea about physical and chemical properties, then names one check that would catch an error or a weak claim in their own work.

student_activity: The learner completes a new application of physical and chemical properties independently and records both the result and the reasoning, evidence, process, or design choice that produced it.
formative_check: In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about physical and chemical properties, then name one check that would catch an error or a weak claim.
scoring_guidance: Score the stated learning target: accuracy, quality of evidence and reasoning, and evidence of checking or revision. Accept any valid approach that meets the criteria. Do not infer effort, motivation, diagnosis, or character from an error. Do not award credit for a numerical result that the learner did not measure, compute, or cite to a named source.
extension_activity: Apply physical and chemical properties under a new constraint, compare two approaches or two sources, or teach the idea with an original example. Extension never means completing another learner's graded work.

hazards.description: Desk-based work only; no chemicals, heat, electricity, or tools are used in this lesson.
hazards.mitigation: Materials are notebook, writing tool, and printed or on-screen text. Any hands-on extension defers to the unit investigation's safety review.

sensitivity: Content is academic; no personal, family, health, or location disclosure is requested.
stop_conditions: Stop for any injury, burn, spill, fume, or allergic reaction and tell the supervising adult.
Stop if a material, tool, or step is not the one this lesson specifies.
Burn: cool it under running cool water for 20 minutes. Do not use ice, butter, or ointment.
Splash in an eye: rinse with running water for 15 minutes, holding the eyelid open, before anything else.
Fumes or a strong smell: leave the room, open a window from outside the room, and do not go back in to tidy up.

Fire: do not use water. Get everyone out, close the door, and call the emergency number. Smother a very small contained flame with a metal pan lid or a fire blanket only if that is safe to do without reaching over it.
If anyone may have swallowed a magnet, a battery, or any material from a lesson, treat it as an emergency and seek medical help at once. Do not wait for symptoms.
A pause, break, or switch to the alternative activity is never treated as failure.
privacy_declarations: Records the learning target, completion state, evidence type, and next step only.
Stores no raw reflection text, no free-text answers, no photograph, no video, and no voice recording.
Requires no camera or video proof of any activity.
Collects no learner body measurement, health measurement, or medical information.
Requires no account creation, purchase, or disclosure of the family's location.

guardian_visibility_note: Share the lesson target, completion state, evidence type, and next instructional step. For any hands-on lesson, share the hazard list, the supervision level, the stop conditions, the safe order, the required PPE, and the disposal steps - including any step that runs unattended or overnight - BEFORE the session so the guardian can review them in advance. Do not expose raw reflections, raw answers, or diagnosis language.
home_connection: Notice one safe, optional example of physical and chemical properties in ordinary life and describe it in a sentence. No purchase, account, photograph, travel, or private disclosure is required, and this is never graded.

value.value: Primary coverage: practice foundation; no performance expectation is claimed for this unit.. Reinforced (already taught in or before this unit, and assessed only where it is primary): HS-ETS1-3.
Learner's own repeated mass and volume trials. Accepted reference densities are looked up for comparison only, after the learner reports their own value.
No special equipment is needed for this lesson; it is notebook and text based. The unit investigation on Day 7 carries the full alternative path.

lesson_flow.title: Safety review before any material is handled
lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action:
READ THIS BEFORE YOU TOUCH ANY MATERIAL.
HAZARD (physical): Looking into a bright light source, or at the sun, damages vision permanently.
MITIGATION: View household lamps only, from at least an arm's length, never the sun and never a laser. No optical device is ever pointed at the sun or at another person. This prohibition is not disableable.
HAZARD (physical): Cutting the viewing slit in the card tube uses a sharp blade.
MITIGATION: An adult cuts the slit; the learner assembles and tapes only. No cutting tool is required of the learner.
SUPERVISION: an adult must be within earshot and able to reach you. Do not start until they are.
SAFE ORDER - do these steps in this order and do not reorder them:
  SAFE ORDER 1. An adult cuts the viewing slit in the card tube; the learner assembles and tapes only.
  SAFE ORDER 2. Tape the CD or grating over the far end and check the tube in a dim room before any bright source is used.
  SAFE ORDER 3. View household lamps only, from at least an arm's length. Never the sun, never a laser, never through any lens toward a bright source.
  SAFE ORDER 4. Sketch each spectrum before comparing it with the published reference images.
  SAFE ORDER 5. Graph the published periodic-trend data and write the predictions down before checking them.
STOP CONDITIONS - stop at once if any of these happens:
  STOP: Stop if any light source is uncomfortable to look toward, and step back.
  STOP: Stop immediately if anyone points the spectroscope, or any lens or grating, toward the sun.
  STOP: Stop for any injury, burn, spill, fume, or allergic reaction and tell the supervising adult.
  STOP: Stop if a material, tool, or step is not the one this lesson specifies.
  STOP: Burn: cool it under running cool water for 20 minutes. Do not use ice, butter, or ointment.
  STOP: Splash in an eye: rinse with running water for 15 minutes, holding the eyelid open, before anything else.
  STOP: Fumes or a strong smell: leave the room, open a window from outside the room, and do not go back in to tidy up.
  STOP: Fire: do not use water. Get everyone out, close the door, and call the emergency number. Smother a very small contained flame with a metal pan lid or a fire blanket only if that is safe to do without reaching over it.
  STOP: If anyone may have swallowed a magnet, a battery, or any material from a lesson, treat it as an emergency and seek medical help at once. Do not wait for symptoms.

materials: table salt
sugar
cooking oil
water
clear plastic cups
spoons
thermometer
STAGE A only: rubbing alcohol (adult-dispensed)
STAGE B only: 9V battery with taped terminals, leads, and a small LED
warm water below 50 degrees Celsius

lesson_flow.title: Safety review before any material is handled
lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action:
READ THIS BEFORE YOU TOUCH ANY MATERIAL.
HAZARD (chemical): Rubbing alcohol is flammable, its vapour is heavier than air and pools at bench level, and it is harmful if swallowed.
MITIGATION: STAGE A runs with no battery, charger, flame, hob, pilot light, heater, or lamp anywhere in the room. An adult dispenses no more than 30 mL per cup, caps the bottle, and removes it from the room at once. Nothing is ever tasted.
HAZARD (chemical): The poured alcohol samples - not just the bottle - are the ignition risk, and a shorting battery is an ignition source.
MITIGATION: STAGE A ends when every POURED SAMPLE is down the drain, the cups washed and dried, and the room ventilated ten minutes - not when the bottle is capped. Only then may a battery enter, and STAGE B runs on a different surface.
HAZARD (chemical): Passing current through salt water is electrolysis: it produces hydrogen at one lead and chlorine gas at the other.
MITIGATION: Each conductivity test is a touch of one to two seconds. Leads are never left standing in a solution. If bubbles form at a lead, disconnect at once, ventilate, and move to the published table.
HAZARD (physical): Battery testing risks a short circuit that heats the leads.
MITIGATION: Use one 9V battery only - NEVER mains electricity, never a lithium or button cell. Keep the LED in the circuit at all times, tape the terminals before and after use, keep leads apart between tests, and let an adult make every connection.
HAZARD (physical): Warm water can scald.
MITIGATION: An adult pours every warm sample and confirms with the thermometer that it reads below 50 degrees Celsius. Temperature is judged with the thermometer, never with a hand.
SUPERVISION: an adult must be beside you, watching, for the whole investigation. Do not start any step until they are there.
EYE PROTECTION IS REQUIRED for this investigation. Put it on before the first step.
SAFE ORDER - do these steps in this order and do not reorder them:
  SAFE ORDER 1. STAGE A and STAGE B never overlap. Stage A is finished and cleared before any battery leaves its packaging.
  SAFE ORDER 2. STAGE A: an adult confirms no battery, charger, flame, hob, pilot light, heater, or lamp is in the room, then pours no more than 30 mL of alcohol into each labelled cup and takes the bottle out of the room.
  SAFE ORDER 3. Observe and record the alcohol solubility results with the bottle gone and no ignition source present.
  SAFE ORDER 4. END OF STAGE A IS A DISPOSAL STEP, NOT A CAPPED BOTTLE: pour every poured alcohol sample down a running cold tap, wash and dry every cup, wipe the tray, and ventilate the room for at least ten minutes.
  SAFE ORDER 5. An adult then confirms out loud that no alcohol - bottle, cup, spill, or smell - is anywhere in the room, and that the surface is dry.
  SAFE ORDER 6. STAGE B runs on a DIFFERENT surface, with water-based samples only. Alcohol is never one of the liquids tested with the battery, and its conductivity is taken from the published table.
  SAFE ORDER 7. An adult builds the circuit with the LED always in it, touches each sample for one to two seconds, and disconnects between tests.
STOP CONDITIONS - stop at once if any of these happens:
  STOP: Stop and put the battery back in its packaging if any cup, spill, or smell of alcohol is still in the room.
  STOP: Never dip a lead, electrode, or wire into alcohol or into any liquid that is not on the STAGE B list.
  STOP: Stop and disconnect if bubbles appear at a lead, if a lead or the battery warms, or if the LED stays lit after a test.
  STOP: Stop if the thermometer reads above 50 degrees Celsius.
  STOP: Never connect anything in this lesson to a wall outlet.
  STOP: Stop for any injury, burn, spill, fume, or allergic reaction and tell the supervising adult.
  STOP: Stop if a material, tool, or step is not the one this lesson specifies.
  STOP: Burn: cool it under running cool water for 20 minutes. Do not use ice, butter, or ointment.
  STOP: Splash in an eye: rinse with running water for 15 minutes, holding the eyelid open, before anything else.
  STOP: Fumes or a strong smell: leave the room, open a window from outside the room, and do not go back in to tidy up.
  STOP: Fire: do not use water. Get everyone out, close the door, and call the emergency number. Smother a very small contained flame with a metal pan lid or a fire blanket only if that is safe to do without reaching over it.
  STOP: If anyone may have swallowed a magnet, a battery, or any material from a lesson, treat it as an emergency and seek medical help at once. Do not wait for symptoms.
  STOP: A pause, break, or switch to the alternative activity is never treated as failure.
DISPOSAL: Alcohol samples go down the drain with the cold tap running at THE END OF STAGE A, before any battery appears; the cups are washed, dried, and put away. Salt, sugar, and oil solutions go down the drain with the tap running after Stage B. Disconnect the battery, tape its terminals, store it away from steel wool and loose metal, and wipe the surface. Nothing from this investigation is ever sealed, capped, or stored while wet. Alcohol and a battery are never left out together at any point.
ALTERNATIVE (equal credit, no special equipment): Compare only salt, sugar, and oil in water at room temperature - solubility and mixing behaviour alone - and take every melting-point and conductivity figure from the published tables. No battery, no alcohol, no heat, and therefore no ignition risk at all. This is the path to choose if the two stages cannot be separated in time and space exactly as written.
ALWAYS - these rules hold in every lesson and nobody can switch them off:
  ALWAYS: Never mix household cleaning products; bleach combined with ammonia or acid releases toxic gas.
  ALWAYS: Never connect any investigation to mains electricity; low-voltage cells only.
  ALWAYS: Never fully seal a reacting, fermenting, oxidising, or warm mixture in any container.
  ALWAYS: Never have a flammable liquid open in the same room as a flame, hob, pilot light, heater, lamp, charger, or battery.
  ALWAYS: Never use alcohol, or any other fuel, for a flame demonstration; no open-flame demonstration is used anywhere in this package.
  ALWAYS: Never light, strike, or operate an open flame or a hob, burner, or pilot light for any investigation in this package; no lesson requires one.
  ALWAYS: Never cut, tear, puncture, or open a sealed commercial product - cold pack, hand warmer, glow stick, or smoke detector.
  ALWAYS: Never look at the sun directly or through any lens, filter, grating, or camera.
  ALWAYS: Never require a photograph, video, or voice recording as evidence of completion.
  ALWAYS: Never request or record a learner body measurement, health measurement, or medical history.
  ALWAYS: Never present invented measurements as real experimental results.

lesson_flow.title: Safety review before any material is handled
lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action:
READ THIS BEFORE YOU TOUCH ANY MATERIAL.
HAZARD (chemical): Rubbing alcohol is flammable, its vapour is heavier than air and pools at bench level, and it is harmful if swallowed.
MITIGATION: STAGE A runs with no battery, charger, flame, hob, pilot light, heater, or lamp anywhere in the room. An adult dispenses no more than 30 mL per cup, caps the bottle, and removes it from the room at once. Nothing is ever tasted.
HAZARD (chemical): The poured alcohol samples - not just the bottle - are the ignition risk, and a shorting battery is an ignition source.
MITIGATION: STAGE A ends when every POURED SAMPLE is down the drain, the cups washed and dried, and the room ventilated ten minutes - not when the bottle is capped. Only then may a battery enter, and STAGE B runs on a different surface.
HAZARD (chemical): Passing current through salt water is electrolysis: it produces hydrogen at one lead and chlorine gas at the other.
MITIGATION: Each conductivity test is a touch of one to two seconds. Leads are never left standing in a solution. If bubbles form at a lead, disconnect at once, ventilate, and move to the published table.
HAZARD (physical): Battery testing risks a short circuit that heats the leads.
MITIGATION: Use one 9V battery only - NEVER mains electricity, never a lithium or button cell. Keep the LED in the circuit at all times, tape the terminals before and after use, keep leads apart between tests, and let an adult make every connection.
HAZARD (physical): Warm water can scald.
MITIGATION: An adult pours every warm sample and confirms with the thermometer that it reads below 50 degrees Celsius. Temperature is judged with the thermometer, never with a hand.
SUPERVISION: an adult must be beside you, watching, for the whole investigation. Do not start any step until they are there.
EYE PROTECTION IS REQUIRED for this investigation. Put it on before the first step.
SAFE ORDER - do these steps in this order and do not reorder them:
  SAFE ORDER 1. STAGE A and STAGE B never overlap. Stage A is finished and cleared before any battery leaves its packaging.
  SAFE ORDER 2. STAGE A: an adult confirms no battery, charger, flame, hob, pilot light, heater, or lamp is in the room, then pours no more than 30 mL of alcohol into each labelled cup and takes the bottle out of the room.
  SAFE ORDER 3. Observe and record the alcohol solubility results with the bottle gone and no ignition source present.
  SAFE ORDER 4. END OF STAGE A IS A DISPOSAL STEP, NOT A CAPPED BOTTLE: pour every poured alcohol sample down a running cold tap, wash and dry every cup, wipe the tray, and ventilate the room for at least ten minutes.
  SAFE ORDER 5. An adult then confirms out loud that no alcohol - bottle, cup, spill, or smell - is anywhere in the room, and that the surface is dry.
  SAFE ORDER 6. STAGE B runs on a DIFFERENT surface, with water-based samples only. Alcohol is never one of the liquids tested with the battery, and its conductivity is taken from the published table.
  SAFE ORDER 7. An adult builds the circuit with the LED always in it, touches each sample for one to two seconds, and disconnects between tests.
STOP CONDITIONS - stop at once if any of these happens:
  STOP: Stop and put the battery back in its packaging if any cup, spill, or smell of alcohol is still in the room.
  STOP: Never dip a lead, electrode, or wire into alcohol or into any liquid that is not on the STAGE B list.
  STOP: Stop and disconnect if bubbles appear at a lead, if a lead or the battery warms, or if the LED stays lit after a test.
  STOP: Stop if the thermometer reads above 50 degrees Celsius.
  STOP: Never connect anything in this lesson to a wall outlet.
  STOP: Stop for any injury, burn, spill, fume, or allergic reaction and tell the supervising adult.
  STOP: Stop if a material, tool, or step is not the one this lesson specifies.
  STOP: Burn: cool it under running cool water for 20 minutes. Do not use ice, butter, or ointment.
  STOP: Splash in an eye: rinse with running water for 15 minutes, holding the eyelid open, before anything else.
  STOP: Fumes or a strong smell: leave the room, open a window from outside the room, and do not go back in to tidy up.
  STOP: Fire: do not use water. Get everyone out, close the door, and call the emergency number. Smother a very small contained flame with a metal pan lid or a fire blanket only if that is safe to do without reaching over it.
  STOP: If anyone may have swallowed a magnet, a battery, or any material from a lesson, treat it as an emergency and seek medical help at once. Do not wait for symptoms.
  STOP: A pause, break, or switch to the alternative activity is never treated as failure.
DISPOSAL: Alcohol samples go down the drain with the cold tap running at THE END OF STAGE A, before any battery appears; the cups are washed, dried, and put away. Salt, sugar, and oil solutions go down the drain with the tap running after Stage B. Disconnect the battery, tape its terminals, store it away from steel wool and loose metal, and wipe the surface. Nothing from this investigation is ever sealed, capped, or stored while wet. Alcohol and a battery are never left out together at any point.
ALTERNATIVE (equal credit, no special equipment): Compare only salt, sugar, and oil in water at room temperature - solubility and mixing behaviour alone - and take every melting-point and conductivity figure from the published tables. No battery, no alcohol, no heat, and therefore no ignition risk at all. This is the path to choose if the two stages cannot be separated in time and space exactly as written.
ALWAYS - these rules hold in every lesson and nobody can switch them off:
  ALWAYS: Never mix household cleaning products; bleach combined with ammonia or acid releases toxic gas.
  ALWAYS: Never connect any investigation to mains electricity; low-voltage cells only.
  ALWAYS: Never fully seal a reacting, fermenting, oxidising, or warm mixture in any container.
  ALWAYS: Never have a flammable liquid open in the same room as a flame, hob, pilot light, heater, lamp, charger, or battery.

lesson_flow.title: Safety review before any material is handled
lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action:
READ THIS BEFORE YOU TOUCH ANY MATERIAL.
HAZARD (chemical): Steel wool in vinegar is an iron-and-acid reaction that slowly releases hydrogen, which is flammable in air across a wide range of concentrations.
MITIGATION: The oxidation run is NEVER put in a bag, jar, or any container with a lid. It stays in a wide open dish in a ventilated room, with no flame, hob, pilot light, heater, battery, charger, or static source anywhere near it.
HAZARD (chemical): Vinegar is a mild acid that stings eyes and open cuts.
MITIGATION: Wear eye protection and gloves, cover any cut with a waterproof dressing, work over a tray, and rinse splashes with water for 15 minutes.
HAZARD (chemical): Combining household chemicals other than those listed can generate toxic gas.
MITIGATION: Use ONLY vinegar, baking soda, and cabbage indicator. Never add bleach, ammonia, drain cleaner, or any cleaning product. This prohibition is not disableable.
HAZARD (physical): Warm water scalds, and household hot taps commonly deliver water above 55 degrees Celsius.
MITIGATION: Cabbage indicator is extracted with water an adult has poured and checked at below 50 degrees Celsius. Hot tap water is never used directly, and temperature is judged with the thermometer, never with a hand.
HAZARD (physical): Steel wool fibres cut skin, and damp finely divided steel wool self-heats as it oxidises.
MITIGATION: Wear gloves. Keep steel wool away from every battery and heat source, and never let it touch a 9V battery from an earlier unit. Warm or damp steel wool is never bagged, boxed, or binned - see the disposal steps.
SUPERVISION: an adult must be beside you, watching, for the whole investigation. Do not start any step until they are there.
EYE PROTECTION IS REQUIRED for this investigation. Put it on before the first step.
SAFE ORDER - do these steps in this order and do not reorder them:
  SAFE ORDER 1. Work in a ventilated room with no flame, hob, pilot light, heater, battery, charger, or spark source present: steel wool in vinegar releases hydrogen, which is flammable.
  SAFE ORDER 2. Put on eye protection and gloves, and cover any cut with a waterproof dressing.
  SAFE ORDER 3. An adult pours the water for the cabbage indicator and confirms with the thermometer that it reads below 50 degrees Celsius. Hot tap water is never used directly.
  SAFE ORDER 4. Make the indicator and complete the vinegar and baking-soda colour work first; that strand uses no steel wool at all.
  SAFE ORDER 5. Weigh the dry steel wool in a disposable tray on the scale - it never touches the scale surface, which stays in food use - then set it in a WIDE OPEN metal or ceramic dish. Never a bag, jar, box, or anything with a lid.
  SAFE ORDER 6. Leave the open dish undisturbed in a ventilated place away from paper, cloth, and anything that can burn, and re-weigh only once it is completely cool and dry.
STOP CONDITIONS - stop at once if any of these happens:
  STOP: Stop immediately if any cleaning product is brought near the work area.
  STOP: Stop if the steel wool or its dish feels warm: leave it open and undisturbed, ventilate the room, and wait until it is cold.
  STOP: Stop if the thermometer reads above 50 degrees Celsius.
  STOP: Never seal, bag, cap, or cover the oxidation run, and never open any inflated container near a flame, hob, or battery.
  STOP: Stop for any injury, burn, spill, fume, or allergic reaction and tell the supervising adult.
  STOP: Stop if a material, tool, or step is not the one this lesson specifies.
  STOP: Burn: cool it under running cool water for 20 minutes. Do not use ice, butter, or ointment.
  STOP: Splash in an eye: rinse with running water for 15 minutes, holding the eyelid open, before anything else.
  STOP: Fumes or a strong smell: leave the room, open a window from outside the room, and do not go back in to tidy up.
  STOP: Fire: do not use water. Get everyone out, close the door, and call the emergency number. Smother a very small contained flame with a metal pan lid or a fire blanket only if that is safe to do without reaching over it.
  STOP: If anyone may have swallowed a magnet, a battery, or any material from a lesson, treat it as an emergency and seek medical help at once. Do not wait for symptoms.
  STOP: A pause, break, or switch to the alternative activity is never treated as failure.
DISPOSAL: NOTHING FROM THIS INVESTIGATION IS EVER SEALED. Leave the steel wool spread out in its open dish, well away from anything combustible, until it is completely cold and dry - normally overnight. Then rinse it under running water until the water runs clear, squeeze it out, and put it into the OUTDOOR waste bin still wet and cold, loose, never bagged and never with paper or a battery. If the dish is warm at any point, stop, leave the room ventilated, and wait. Pour the vinegar, baking-soda, and cabbage solutions down the drain with the tap running. Bin the disposable weighing tray; it never returns to food use.
ALTERNATIVE (equal credit, no special equipment): Run the cabbage-indicator colour scale with vinegar and baking soda only - no steel wool, no hydrogen, no cool-down - and analyse published mass-change data for the rusting reaction. Kitchen materials only. This is the path to choose if the household cannot leave an open dish ventilated and undisturbed overnight.
ALWAYS - these rules hold in every lesson and nobody can switch them off:
  ALWAYS: Never mix household cleaning products; bleach combined with ammonia or acid releases toxic gas.
  ALWAYS: Never connect any investigation to mains electricity; low-voltage cells only.
  ALWAYS: Never fully seal a reacting, fermenting, oxidising, or warm mixture in any container.
  ALWAYS: Never have a flammable liquid open in the same room as a flame, hob, pilot light, heater, lamp, charger, or battery.
  ALWAYS: Never use alcohol, or any other fuel, for a flame demonstration; no open-flame demonstration is used anywhere in this package.
  ALWAYS: Never light, strike, or operate an open flame or a hob, burner, or pilot light for any investigation in this package; no lesson requires one.
  ALWAYS: Never cut, tear, puncture, or open a sealed commercial product - cold pack, hand warmer, glow stick, or smoke detector.
  ALWAYS: Never look at the sun directly or through any lens, filter, grating, or camera.
  ALWAYS: Never require a photograph, video, or voice recording as evidence of completion.
  ALWAYS: Never request or record a learner body measurement, health measurement, or medical history.
  ALWAYS: Never present invented measurements as real experimental results.

lesson_flow.title: Safety review before any material is handled
lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action:
READ THIS BEFORE YOU TOUCH ANY MATERIAL.
HAZARD (chemical): Steel wool in vinegar is an iron-and-acid reaction that slowly releases hydrogen, which is flammable in air across a wide range of concentrations.
MITIGATION: The oxidation run is NEVER put in a bag, jar, or any container with a lid. It stays in a wide open dish in a ventilated room, with no flame, hob, pilot light, heater, battery, charger, or static source anywhere near it.
HAZARD (chemical): Vinegar is a mild acid that stings eyes and open cuts.
MITIGATION: Wear eye protection and gloves, cover any cut with a waterproof dressing, work over a tray, and rinse splashes with water for 15 minutes.
HAZARD (chemical): Combining household chemicals other than those listed can generate toxic gas.
MITIGATION: Use ONLY vinegar, baking soda, and cabbage indicator. Never add bleach, ammonia, drain cleaner, or any cleaning product. This prohibition is not disableable.
HAZARD (physical): Warm water scalds, and household hot taps commonly deliver water above 55 degrees Celsius.
MITIGATION: Cabbage indicator is extracted with water an adult has poured and checked at below 50 degrees Celsius. Hot tap water is never used directly, and temperature is judged with the thermometer, never with a hand.
HAZARD (physical): Steel wool fibres cut skin, and damp finely divided steel wool self-heats as it oxidises.
MITIGATION: Wear gloves. Keep steel wool away from every battery and heat source, and never let it touch a 9V battery from an earlier unit. Warm or damp steel wool is never bagged, boxed, or binned - see the disposal steps.
SUPERVISION: an adult must be beside you, watching, for the whole investigation. Do not start any step until they are there.
EYE PROTECTION IS REQUIRED for this investigation. Put it on before the first step.
SAFE ORDER - do these steps in this order and do not reorder them:
  SAFE ORDER 1. Work in a ventilated room with no flame, hob, pilot light, heater, battery, charger, or spark source present: steel wool in vinegar releases hydrogen, which is flammable.
  SAFE ORDER 2. Put on eye protection and gloves, and cover any cut with a waterproof dressing.
  SAFE ORDER 3. An adult pours the water for the cabbage indicator and confirms with the thermometer that it reads below 50 degrees Celsius. Hot tap water is never used directly.
  SAFE ORDER 4. Make the indicator and complete the vinegar and baking-soda colour work first; that strand uses no steel wool at all.
  SAFE ORDER 5. Weigh the dry steel wool in a disposable tray on the scale - it never touches the scale surface, which stays in food use - then set it in a WIDE OPEN metal or ceramic dish. Never a bag, jar, box, or anything with a lid.
  SAFE ORDER 6. Leave the open dish undisturbed in a ventilated place away from paper, cloth, and anything that can burn, and re-weigh only once it is completely cool and dry.
STOP CONDITIONS - stop at once if any of these happens:
  STOP: Stop immediately if any cleaning product is brought near the work area.
  STOP: Stop if the steel wool or its dish feels warm: leave it open and undisturbed, ventilate the room, and wait until it is cold.
  STOP: Stop if the thermometer reads above 50 degrees Celsius.
  STOP: Never seal, bag, cap, or cover the oxidation run, and never open any inflated container near a flame, hob, or battery.
  STOP: Stop for any injury, burn, spill, fume, or allergic reaction and tell the supervising adult.
  STOP: Stop if a material, tool, or step is not the one this lesson specifies.
  STOP: Burn: cool it under running cool water for 20 minutes. Do not use ice, butter, or ointment.
  STOP: Splash in an eye: rinse with running water for 15 minutes, holding the eyelid open, before anything else.
  STOP: Fumes or a strong smell: leave the room, open a window from outside the room, and do not go back in to tidy up.
  STOP: Fire: do not use water. Get everyone out, close the door, and call the emergency number. Smother a very small contained flame with a metal pan lid or a fire blanket only if that is safe to do without reaching over it.
  STOP: If anyone may have swallowed a magnet, a battery, or any material from a lesson, treat it as an emergency and seek medical help at once. Do not wait for symptoms.
  STOP: A pause, break, or switch to the alternative activity is never treated as failure.
DISPOSAL: NOTHING FROM THIS INVESTIGATION IS EVER SEALED. Leave the steel wool spread out in its open dish, well away from anything combustible, until it is completely cold and dry - normally overnight. Then rinse it under running water until the water runs clear, squeeze it out, and put it into the OUTDOOR waste bin still wet and cold, loose, never bagged and never with paper or a battery. If the dish is warm at any point, stop, leave the room ventilated, and wait. Pour the vinegar, baking-soda, and cabbage solutions down the drain with the tap running. Bin the disposable weighing tray; it never returns to food use.
ALTERNATIVE (equal credit, no special equipment): Run the cabbage-indicator colour scale with vinegar and baking soda only - no steel wool, no hydrogen, no cool-down - and analyse published mass-change data for the rusting reaction. Kitchen materials only. This is the path to choose if the household cannot leave an open dish ventilated and undisturbed overnight.
ALWAYS - these rules hold in every lesson and nobody can switch them off:
  ALWAYS: Never mix household cleaning products; bleach combined with ammonia or acid releases toxic gas.
  ALWAYS: Never connect any investigation to mains electricity; low-voltage cells only.
  ALWAYS: Never fully seal a reacting, fermenting, oxidising, or warm mixture in any container.
  ALWAYS: Never have a flammable liquid open in the same room as a flame, hob, pilot light, heater, lamp, charger, or battery.
  ALWAYS: Never use alcohol, or any other fuel, for a flame demonstration; no open-flame demonstration is used anywhere in this package.
  ALWAYS: Never light, strike, or operate an open flame or a hob, burner, or pilot light for any investigation in this package; no lesson requires one.
  ALWAYS: Never cut, tear, puncture, or open a sealed commercial product - cold pack, hand warmer, glow stick, or smoke detector.
  ALWAYS: Never look at the sun directly or through any lens, filter, grating, or camera.
  ALWAYS: Never require a photograph, video, or voice recording as evidence of completion.
  ALWAYS: Never request or record a learner body measurement, health measurement, or medical history.
  ALWAYS: Never present invented measurements as real experimental results.

lesson_flow.title: Safety review before any material is handled
lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action:
READ THIS BEFORE YOU TOUCH ANY MATERIAL.
HAZARD (chemical): Vinegar stings eyes, and the reaction produces carbon dioxide.
MITIGATION: Wear eye protection and work in a ventilated room. At the quantities fixed below the carbon dioxide is harmless; the quantities are what keep it that way, so they are part of the procedure and not a suggestion.
HAZARD (physical): A closed bag holding a gas-producing reaction can burst and spray liquid.
MITIGATION: The closed trial is SEALED COMPLETELY - a part-sealed bag is not a closed system - and is made safe by volume: half a teaspoon of baking soda and 20 mL of vinegar in a one-litre bag. Flat on a tray, pointed away, never held.
SUPERVISION: an adult must be beside you, watching, for the whole investigation. Do not start any step until they are there.
EYE PROTECTION IS REQUIRED for this investigation. Put it on before the first step.
SAFE ORDER - do these steps in this order and do not reorder them:
  SAFE ORDER 1. Work over a tray in a ventilated room with eye protection on.
  SAFE ORDER 2. Run the OPEN system first: weigh the cup of vinegar and the separate baking soda, combine them, and re-weigh once fizzing has stopped.
  SAFE ORDER 3. For the CLOSED system measure exactly: no more than half a teaspoon of baking soda and 20 mL of vinegar, in a one-litre freezer bag with the air pressed out.
  SAFE ORDER 4. SEAL THE BAG COMPLETELY. A part-sealed bag is not a closed system and cannot answer this unit's question; the small quantity and the free space, not a loose seal, are what keep it safe.
  SAFE ORDER 5. Lay the sealed bag flat on the tray at arm's length, pointed away from every face. Never hold, squeeze, or lift it while it reacts.
  SAFE ORDER 6. Weigh it without lifting it off the tray, and wait until fizzing has completely stopped before opening a corner.
STOP CONDITIONS - stop at once if any of these happens:
  STOP: Stop, do not touch the bag, and let an adult carry the whole tray outdoors if the bag becomes firm or taut.
  STOP: Stop if the quantities on the materials list cannot be measured accurately, and run the published-data path instead.
  STOP: Stop if liquid contacts the eyes and rinse for 15 minutes.
  STOP: Stop for any injury, burn, spill, fume, or allergic reaction and tell the supervising adult.
  STOP: Stop if a material, tool, or step is not the one this lesson specifies.
  STOP: Burn: cool it under running cool water for 20 minutes. Do not use ice, butter, or ointment.
  STOP: Splash in an eye: rinse with running water for 15 minutes, holding the eyelid open, before anything else.
  STOP: Fumes or a strong smell: leave the room, open a window from outside the room, and do not go back in to tidy up.
  STOP: Fire: do not use water. Get everyone out, close the door, and call the emergency number. Smother a very small contained flame with a metal pan lid or a fire blanket only if that is safe to do without reaching over it.
  STOP: If anyone may have swallowed a magnet, a battery, or any material from a lesson, treat it as an emergency and seek medical help at once. Do not wait for symptoms.
  STOP: A pause, break, or switch to the alternative activity is never treated as failure.
DISPOSAL: Open the bag by one corner only, over the sink, away from every face; pour the contents down the drain with the tap running and rinse the bag before recycling or binning it. Wipe the tray and wash hands. Never re-seal a bag that still holds gas, and never store a sealed bag from this investigation.
ALTERNATIVE (equal credit, no special equipment): Do the mass accounting from a supplied table of published open- and closed-system masses, balancing the equation and computing expected gas mass by hand. Paper and calculator only.
ALWAYS - these rules hold in every lesson and nobody can switch them off:
  ALWAYS: Never mix household cleaning products; bleach combined with ammonia or acid releases toxic gas.
  ALWAYS: Never connect any investigation to mains electricity; low-voltage cells only.
  ALWAYS: Never fully seal a reacting, fermenting, oxidising, or warm mixture in any container.
  ALWAYS: Never have a flammable liquid open in the same room as a flame, hob, pilot light, heater, lamp, charger, or battery.
  ALWAYS: Never use alcohol, or any other fuel, for a flame demonstration; no open-flame demonstration is used anywhere in this package.
  ALWAYS: Never light, strike, or operate an open flame or a hob, burner, or pilot light for any investigation in this package; no lesson requires one.
  ALWAYS: Never cut, tear, puncture, or open a sealed commercial product - cold pack, hand warmer, glow stick, or smoke detector.
  ALWAYS: Never look at the sun directly or through any lens, filter, grating, or camera.
  ALWAYS: Never require a photograph, video, or voice recording as evidence of completion.
  ALWAYS: Never request or record a learner body measurement, health measurement, or medical history.
  ALWAYS: Never present invented measurements as real experimental results.

lesson_flow.title: Safety review before any material is handled
lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action:
READ THIS BEFORE YOU TOUCH ANY MATERIAL.
HAZARD (chemical): Vinegar stings eyes, and the reaction produces carbon dioxide.
MITIGATION: Wear eye protection and work in a ventilated room. At the quantities fixed below the carbon dioxide is harmless; the quantities are what keep it that way, so they are part of the procedure and not a suggestion.
HAZARD (physical): A closed bag holding a gas-producing reaction can burst and spray liquid.
MITIGATION: The closed trial is SEALED COMPLETELY - a part-sealed bag is not a closed system - and is made safe by volume: half a teaspoon of baking soda and 20 mL of vinegar in a one-litre bag. Flat on a tray, pointed away, never held.
SUPERVISION: an adult must be beside you, watching, for the whole investigation. Do not start any step until they are there.
EYE PROTECTION IS REQUIRED for this investigation. Put it on before the first step.
SAFE ORDER - do these steps in this order and do not reorder them:
  SAFE ORDER 1. Work over a tray in a ventilated room with eye protection on.
  SAFE ORDER 2. Run the OPEN system first: weigh the cup of vinegar and the separate baking soda, combine them, and re-weigh once fizzing has stopped.
  SAFE ORDER 3. For the CLOSED system measure exactly: no more than half a teaspoon of baking soda and 20 mL of vinegar, in a one-litre freezer bag with the air pressed out.
  SAFE ORDER 4. SEAL THE BAG COMPLETELY. A part-sealed bag is not a closed system and cannot answer this unit's question; the small quantity and the free space, not a loose seal, are what keep it safe.
  SAFE ORDER 5. Lay the sealed bag flat on the tray at arm's length, pointed away from every face. Never hold, squeeze, or lift it while it reacts.
  SAFE ORDER 6. Weigh it without lifting it off the tray, and wait until fizzing has completely stopped before opening a corner.
STOP CONDITIONS - stop at once if any of these happens:
  STOP: Stop, do not touch the bag, and let an adult carry the whole tray outdoors if the bag becomes firm or taut.
  STOP: Stop if the quantities on the materials list cannot be measured accurately, and run the published-data path instead.
  STOP: Stop if liquid contacts the eyes and rinse for 15 minutes.
  STOP: Stop for any injury, burn, spill, fume, or allergic reaction and tell the supervising adult.
  STOP: Stop if a material, tool, or step is not the one this lesson specifies.
  STOP: Burn: cool it under running cool water for 20 minutes. Do not use ice, butter, or ointment.
  STOP: Splash in an eye: rinse with running water for 15 minutes, holding the eyelid open, before anything else.
  STOP: Fumes or a strong smell: leave the room, open a window from outside the room, and do not go back in to tidy up.
  STOP: Fire: do not use water. Get everyone out, close the door, and call the emergency number. Smother a very small contained flame with a metal pan lid or a fire blanket only if that is safe to do without reaching over it.
  STOP: If anyone may have swallowed a magnet, a battery, or any material from a lesson, treat it as an emergency and seek medical help at once. Do not wait for symptoms.
  STOP: A pause, break, or switch to the alternative activity is never treated as failure.
DISPOSAL: Open the bag by one corner only, over the sink, away from every face; pour the contents down the drain with the tap running and rinse the bag before recycling or binning it. Wipe the tray and wash hands. Never re-seal a bag that still holds gas, and never store a sealed bag from this investigation.
ALTERNATIVE (equal credit, no special equipment): Do the mass accounting from a supplied table of published open- and closed-system masses, balancing the equation and computing expected gas mass by hand. Paper and calculator only.
ALWAYS - these rules hold in every lesson and nobody can switch them off:
  ALWAYS: Never mix household cleaning products; bleach combined with ammonia or acid releases toxic gas.
  ALWAYS: Never connect any investigation to mains electricity; low-voltage cells only.
  ALWAYS: Never fully seal a reacting, fermenting, oxidising, or warm mixture in any container.
  ALWAYS: Never have a flammable liquid open in the same room as a flame, hob, pilot light, heater, lamp, charger, or battery.
  ALWAYS: Never use alcohol, or any other fuel, for a flame demonstration; no open-flame demonstration is used anywhere in this package.
  ALWAYS: Never light, strike, or operate an open flame or a hob, burner, or pilot light for any investigation in this package; no lesson requires one.
  ALWAYS: Never cut, tear, puncture, or open a sealed commercial product - cold pack, hand warmer, glow stick, or smoke detector.
  ALWAYS: Never look at the sun directly or through any lens, filter, grating, or camera.
  ALWAYS: Never require a photograph, video, or voice recording as evidence of completion.
  ALWAYS: Never request or record a learner body measurement, health measurement, or medical history.
  ALWAYS: Never present invented measurements as real experimental results.

lesson_flow.title: Safety review before any material is handled
lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action:
READ THIS BEFORE YOU TOUCH ANY MATERIAL.
HAZARD (chemical): A cold pack holds a salt that irritates skin and eyes and is harmful if swallowed; a torn hand warmer releases self-heating iron powder reaching about 65 degrees Celsius, an inhalation and ignition hazard.
MITIGATION: OBSERVED FROM THE OUTSIDE ONLY: never cut, torn, punctured, or opened, and the contents never touched or tasted. If one leaks, an adult bags and bins it and contact is rinsed 15 minutes. Not disableable.
HAZARD (chemical): Calcium chloride releases substantial heat when dissolving and can burn skin and eyes, and pouring water onto the solid spatters hot solution.
MITIGATION: OPTIONAL. An adult handles the solid from its original labelled container - never bulk road salt. Eye protection and gloves; under one teaspoon; SOLID IS ALWAYS ADDED TO THE WATER, never the reverse; never touched warm.
HAZARD (chemical): Ice-melt calcium chloride is not a food grade and leaves residue on whatever holds, stirs, or measures it.
MITIGATION: The calcium chloride route runs in disposable cups with a disposable stirrer, binned after one use. No mug, tumbler, flask, bottle, or drinking cup holds it, and nothing that touches it returns to food or drinking use.
HAZARD (physical): Solutions can become hot enough to burn.
MITIGATION: Use an insulated cup on a tray, stir with the thermometer rather than a finger, judge temperature only from the thermometer, and stop if the solution exceeds 50 degrees Celsius.
SUPERVISION: an adult must be beside you, watching, for the whole investigation. Do not start any step until they are there.
EYE PROTECTION IS REQUIRED for this investigation. Put it on before the first step.
SAFE ORDER - do these steps in this order and do not reorder them:
  SAFE ORDER 1. Read the phenomenon with the commercial cold pack and hand warmer SEALED. They are squeezed and felt through the pouch only, and are never cut, torn, punctured, or opened.
  SAFE ORDER 2. Put on eye protection; if the calcium chloride route runs, put on gloves too and let the adult handle the solid from its original labelled container.
  SAFE ORDER 3. If the calcium chloride route runs, set out its DISPOSABLE cups and stirrer now. Calcium chloride is never put in a mug, tumbler, flask, bottle, or drinking cup, and nothing that touches it returns to food or drinking use.
  SAFE ORDER 4. Set the insulated cup on a tray and record the starting temperature before anything is added.
  SAFE ORDER 5. ALWAYS ADD THE SOLID TO THE WATER, a little at a time, never water to the solid. Keep every quantity under one teaspoon.
  SAFE ORDER 6. Stir with the thermometer, not a finger, and read temperature only from the thermometer.
  SAFE ORDER 7. Stop at 50 degrees Celsius and let the solution stand untouched until it is cool.
STOP CONDITIONS - stop at once if any of these happens:
  STOP: Stop if anyone cuts, tears, punctures, or opens a commercial cold pack or hand warmer.
  STOP: Stop if the thermometer reads above 50 degrees Celsius.
  STOP: Stop if calcium chloride contacts skin and rinse thoroughly for 15 minutes.
  STOP: Skip the calcium chloride route entirely if eye protection and gloves are not available.
  STOP: Stop for any injury, burn, spill, fume, or allergic reaction and tell the supervising adult.
  STOP: Stop if a material, tool, or step is not the one this lesson specifies.
  STOP: Burn: cool it under running cool water for 20 minutes. Do not use ice, butter, or ointment.
  STOP: Splash in an eye: rinse with running water for 15 minutes, holding the eyelid open, before anything else.
  STOP: Fumes or a strong smell: leave the room, open a window from outside the room, and do not go back in to tidy up.
  STOP: Fire: do not use water. Get everyone out, close the door, and call the emergency number. Smother a very small contained flame with a metal pan lid or a fire blanket only if that is safe to do without reaching over it.
  STOP: If anyone may have swallowed a magnet, a battery, or any material from a lesson, treat it as an emergency and seek medical help at once. Do not wait for symptoms.
  STOP: A pause, break, or switch to the alternative activity is never treated as failure.
DISPOSAL: Let every solution cool to room temperature in its OPEN cup before it is moved; never cap or store a warm solution. Pour cooled Epsom-salt, baking-soda, and vinegar solutions down the drain with the tap running. Dilute a cooled calcium chloride solution with plenty of cold water as it goes down the drain, then bin the disposable cups and stirrer that held it; they never return to food or drinking use. The cold pack and the hand warmer go into the household bin STILL SEALED - never opened, drained, or cut.
ALTERNATIVE (equal credit, no special equipment): Use Epsom salt and baking soda with vinegar only - both mild - to observe cooling and mild warming, or work entirely from a published table of dissolution enthalpies and bond energies. Kitchen materials or paper.
ALWAYS - these rules hold in every lesson and nobody can switch them off:
  ALWAYS: Never mix household cleaning products; bleach combined with ammonia or acid releases toxic gas.
  ALWAYS: Never connect any investigation to mains electricity; low-voltage cells only.
  ALWAYS: Never fully seal a reacting, fermenting, oxidising, or warm mixture in any container.
  ALWAYS: Never have a flammable liquid open in the same room as a flame, hob, pilot light, heater, lamp, charger, or battery.
  ALWAYS: Never use alcohol, or any other fuel, for a flame demonstration; no open-flame demonstration is used anywhere in this package.
  ALWAYS: Never light, strike, or operate an open flame or a hob, burner, or pilot light for any investigation in this package; no lesson requires one.
  ALWAYS: Never cut, tear, puncture, or open a sealed commercial product - cold pack, hand warmer, glow stick, or smoke detector.
  ALWAYS: Never look at the sun directly or through any lens, filter, grating, or camera.
  ALWAYS: Never require a photograph, video, or voice recording as evidence of completion.
  ALWAYS: Never request or record a learner body measurement, health measurement, or medical history.
  ALWAYS: Never present invented measurements as real experimental results.

lesson_flow.title: Safety review before any material is handled
lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action:
READ THIS BEFORE YOU TOUCH ANY MATERIAL.
HAZARD (chemical): A cold pack holds a salt that irritates skin and eyes and is harmful if swallowed; a torn hand warmer releases self-heating iron powder reaching about 65 degrees Celsius, an inhalation and ignition hazard.
MITIGATION: OBSERVED FROM THE OUTSIDE ONLY: never cut, torn, punctured, or opened, and the contents never touched or tasted. If one leaks, an adult bags and bins it and contact is rinsed 15 minutes. Not disableable.
HAZARD (chemical): Calcium chloride releases substantial heat when dissolving and can burn skin and eyes, and pouring water onto the solid spatters hot solution.
MITIGATION: OPTIONAL. An adult handles the solid from its original labelled container - never bulk road salt. Eye protection and gloves; under one teaspoon; SOLID IS ALWAYS ADDED TO THE WATER, never the reverse; never touched warm.
HAZARD (chemical): Ice-melt calcium chloride is not a food grade and leaves residue on whatever holds, stirs, or measures it.
MITIGATION: The calcium chloride route runs in disposable cups with a disposable stirrer, binned after one use. No mug, tumbler, flask, bottle, or drinking cup holds it, and nothing that touches it returns to food or drinking use.
HAZARD (physical): Solutions can become hot enough to burn.
MITIGATION: Use an insulated cup on a tray, stir with the thermometer rather than a finger, judge temperature only from the thermometer, and stop if the solution exceeds 50 degrees Celsius.
SUPERVISION: an adult must be beside you, watching, for the whole investigation. Do not start any step until they are there.
EYE PROTECTION IS REQUIRED for this investigation. Put it on before the first step.
SAFE ORDER - do these steps in this order and do not reorder them:
  SAFE ORDER 1. Read the phenomenon with the commercial cold pack and hand warmer SEALED. They are squeezed and felt through the pouch only, and are never cut, torn, punctured, or opened.
  SAFE ORDER 2. Put on eye protection; if the calcium chloride route runs, put on gloves too and let the adult handle the solid from its original labelled container.
  SAFE ORDER 3. If the calcium chloride route runs, set out its DISPOSABLE cups and stirrer now. Calcium chloride is never put in a mug, tumbler, flask, bottle, or drinking cup, and nothing that touches it returns to food or drinking use.
  SAFE ORDER 4. Set the insulated cup on a tray and record the starting temperature before anything is added.
  SAFE ORDER 5. ALWAYS ADD THE SOLID TO THE WATER, a little at a time, never water to the solid. Keep every quantity under one teaspoon.
  SAFE ORDER 6. Stir with the thermometer, not a finger, and read temperature only from the thermometer.
  SAFE ORDER 7. Stop at 50 degrees Celsius and let the solution stand untouched until it is cool.
STOP CONDITIONS - stop at once if any of these happens:
  STOP: Stop if anyone cuts, tears, punctures, or opens a commercial cold pack or hand warmer.
  STOP: Stop if the thermometer reads above 50 degrees Celsius.
  STOP: Stop if calcium chloride contacts skin and rinse thoroughly for 15 minutes.
  STOP: Skip the calcium chloride route entirely if eye protection and gloves are not available.
  STOP: Stop for any injury, burn, spill, fume, or allergic reaction and tell the supervising adult.
  STOP: Stop if a material, tool, or step is not the one this lesson specifies.
  STOP: Burn: cool it under running cool water for 20 minutes. Do not use ice, butter, or ointment.
  STOP: Splash in an eye: rinse with running water for 15 minutes, holding the eyelid open, before anything else.
  STOP: Fumes or a strong smell: leave the room, open a window from outside the room, and do not go back in to tidy up.
  STOP: Fire: do not use water. Get everyone out, close the door, and call the emergency number. Smother a very small contained flame with a metal pan lid or a fire blanket only if that is safe to do without reaching over it.
  STOP: If anyone may have swallowed a magnet, a battery, or any material from a lesson, treat it as an emergency and seek medical help at once. Do not wait for symptoms.
  STOP: A pause, break, or switch to the alternative activity is never treated as failure.
DISPOSAL: Let every solution cool to room temperature in its OPEN cup before it is moved; never cap or store a warm solution. Pour cooled Epsom-salt, baking-soda, and vinegar solutions down the drain with the tap running. Dilute a cooled calcium chloride solution with plenty of cold water as it goes down the drain, then bin the disposable cups and stirrer that held it; they never return to food or drinking use. The cold pack and the hand warmer go into the household bin STILL SEALED - never opened, drained, or cut.
ALTERNATIVE (equal credit, no special equipment): Use Epsom salt and baking soda with vinegar only - both mild - to observe cooling and mild warming, or work entirely from a published table of dissolution enthalpies and bond energies. Kitchen materials or paper.
ALWAYS - these rules hold in every lesson and nobody can switch them off:
  ALWAYS: Never mix household cleaning products; bleach combined with ammonia or acid releases toxic gas.
  ALWAYS: Never connect any investigation to mains electricity; low-voltage cells only.
  ALWAYS: Never fully seal a reacting, fermenting, oxidising, or warm mixture in any container.
  ALWAYS: Never have a flammable liquid open in the same room as a flame, hob, pilot light, heater, lamp, charger, or battery.
  ALWAYS: Never use alcohol, or any other fuel, for a flame demonstration; no open-flame demonstration is used anywhere in this package.
  ALWAYS: Never light, strike, or operate an open flame or a hob, burner, or pilot light for any investigation in this package; no lesson requires one.
  ALWAYS: Never cut, tear, puncture, or open a sealed commercial product - cold pack, hand warmer, glow stick, or smoke detector.
  ALWAYS: Never look at the sun directly or through any lens, filter, grating, or camera.
  ALWAYS: Never require a photograph, video, or voice recording as evidence of completion.
  ALWAYS: Never request or record a learner body measurement, health measurement, or medical history.
  ALWAYS: Never present invented measurements as real experimental results.

lesson_flow.title: Safety review before any material is handled
lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action:
READ THIS BEFORE YOU TOUCH ANY MATERIAL.
HAZARD (chemical): A glow stick holds an internal glass ampoule, irritant esters, and hydrogen peroxide.
MITIGATION: Bend to activate; never cut, bite, open, or mouth a glow stick. If one splits, nobody touches it: rinse any contact 15 minutes and an adult bags and bins it. This prohibition is not disableable.
HAZARD (chemical): Vinegar and effervescent tablets irritate eyes.
MITIGATION: Wear eye protection, work over a tray, and rinse splashes with water.
HAZARD (physical): Warm water can scald and glass can break with thermal shock.
MITIGATION: An adult pours every warm sample and confirms with the thermometer that it reads below 50 degrees Celsius. Use plastic or unbreakable cups only.
SUPERVISION: an adult must be beside you, watching, for the whole investigation. Do not start any step until they are there.
EYE PROTECTION IS REQUIRED for this investigation. Put it on before the first step.
SAFE ORDER - do these steps in this order and do not reorder them:
  SAFE ORDER 1. Bend the glow stick to activate it; never cut, bite, or open one, and never put one in a mouth.
  SAFE ORDER 2. An adult prepares the warm water and confirms with the thermometer that it reads below 50 degrees Celsius before any cup is placed.
  SAFE ORDER 3. Put on eye protection and set every cup on a tray.
  SAFE ORDER 4. Run one condition at a time, from cold to warm, recording each timing before anything is changed.
  SAFE ORDER 5. Never cap, seal, or cover a cup while it is fizzing.
STOP CONDITIONS - stop at once if any of these happens:
  STOP: Stop if the thermometer reads above 50 degrees Celsius. Water temperature is judged with the thermometer, never with a hand.
  STOP: Stop if a glow stick splits or leaks, and let an adult bag and bin it.
  STOP: Never seal, cap, or cover a container during an effervescent reaction.
  STOP: Stop for any injury, burn, spill, fume, or allergic reaction and tell the supervising adult.
  STOP: Stop if a material, tool, or step is not the one this lesson specifies.
  STOP: Burn: cool it under running cool water for 20 minutes. Do not use ice, butter, or ointment.
  STOP: Splash in an eye: rinse with running water for 15 minutes, holding the eyelid open, before anything else.
  STOP: Fumes or a strong smell: leave the room, open a window from outside the room, and do not go back in to tidy up.
  STOP: Fire: do not use water. Get everyone out, close the door, and call the emergency number. Smother a very small contained flame with a metal pan lid or a fire blanket only if that is safe to do without reaching over it.
  STOP: If anyone may have swallowed a magnet, a battery, or any material from a lesson, treat it as an emergency and seek medical help at once. Do not wait for symptoms.
  STOP: A pause, break, or switch to the alternative activity is never treated as failure.
DISPOSAL: Pour all vinegar and effervescent solutions down the drain with the tap running, rinse and dry the cups, and wipe the tray. A cup is never sealed, capped, or covered while it is still fizzing. A spent glow stick goes into the household bin intact. If one has split or leaked, nobody touches it: an adult bags it and bins it and any contact is rinsed for 15 minutes.
ALTERNATIVE (equal credit, no special equipment): Vary only surface area and concentration at room temperature - whole versus crushed tablet, full-strength versus diluted vinegar - eliminating all heating. Or analyse a published rate-versus-temperature dataset. Kitchen materials or paper.
ALWAYS - these rules hold in every lesson and nobody can switch them off:
  ALWAYS: Never mix household cleaning products; bleach combined with ammonia or acid releases toxic gas.
  ALWAYS: Never connect any investigation to mains electricity; low-voltage cells only.
  ALWAYS: Never fully seal a reacting, fermenting, oxidising, or warm mixture in any container.
  ALWAYS: Never have a flammable liquid open in the same room as a flame, hob, pilot light, heater, lamp, charger, or battery.
  ALWAYS: Never use alcohol, or any other fuel, for a flame demonstration; no open-flame demonstration is used anywhere in this package.
  ALWAYS: Never light, strike, or operate an open flame or a hob, burner, or pilot light for any investigation in this package; no lesson requires one.
  ALWAYS: Never cut, tear, puncture, or open a sealed commercial product - cold pack, hand warmer, glow stick, or smoke detector.
  ALWAYS: Never look at the sun directly or through any lens, filter, grating, or camera.
  ALWAYS: Never require a photograph, video, or voice recording as evidence of completion.
  ALWAYS: Never request or record a learner body measurement, health measurement, or medical history.
  ALWAYS: Never present invented measurements as real experimental results.

lesson_flow.title: Safety review before any material is handled
lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action:
READ THIS BEFORE YOU TOUCH ANY MATERIAL.
HAZARD (chemical): A glow stick holds an internal glass ampoule, irritant esters, and hydrogen peroxide.
MITIGATION: Bend to activate; never cut, bite, open, or mouth a glow stick. If one splits, nobody touches it: rinse any contact 15 minutes and an adult bags and bins it. This prohibition is not disableable.
HAZARD (chemical): Vinegar and effervescent tablets irritate eyes.
MITIGATION: Wear eye protection, work over a tray, and rinse splashes with water.
HAZARD (physical): Warm water can scald and glass can break with thermal shock.
MITIGATION: An adult pours every warm sample and confirms with the thermometer that it reads below 50 degrees Celsius. Use plastic or unbreakable cups only.
SUPERVISION: an adult must be beside you, watching, for the whole investigation. Do not start any step until they are there.
EYE PROTECTION IS REQUIRED for this investigation. Put it on before the first step.
SAFE ORDER - do these steps in this order and do not reorder them:
  SAFE ORDER 1. Bend the glow stick to activate it; never cut, bite, or open one, and never put one in a mouth.
  SAFE ORDER 2. An adult prepares the warm water and confirms with the thermometer that it reads below 50 degrees Celsius before any cup is placed.
  SAFE ORDER 3. Put on eye protection and set every cup on a tray.
  SAFE ORDER 4. Run one condition at a time, from cold to warm, recording each timing before anything is changed.
  SAFE ORDER 5. Never cap, seal, or cover a cup while it is fizzing.
STOP CONDITIONS - stop at once if any of these happens:
  STOP: Stop if the thermometer reads above 50 degrees Celsius. Water temperature is judged with the thermometer, never with a hand.
  STOP: Stop if a glow stick splits or leaks, and let an adult bag and bin it.
  STOP: Never seal, cap, or cover a container during an effervescent reaction.
  STOP: Stop for any injury, burn, spill, fume, or allergic reaction and tell the supervising adult.
  STOP: Stop if a material, tool, or step is not the one this lesson specifies.
  STOP: Burn: cool it under running cool water for 20 minutes. Do not use ice, butter, or ointment.
  STOP: Splash in an eye: rinse with running water for 15 minutes, holding the eyelid open, before anything else.
  STOP: Fumes or a strong smell: leave the room, open a window from outside the room, and do not go back in to tidy up.
  STOP: Fire: do not use water. Get everyone out, close the door, and call the emergency number. Smother a very small contained flame with a metal pan lid or a fire blanket only if that is safe to do without reaching over it.
  STOP: If anyone may have swallowed a magnet, a battery, or any material from a lesson, treat it as an emergency and seek medical help at once. Do not wait for symptoms.
  STOP: A pause, break, or switch to the alternative activity is never treated as failure.
DISPOSAL: Pour all vinegar and effervescent solutions down the drain with the tap running, rinse and dry the cups, and wipe the tray. A cup is never sealed, capped, or covered while it is still fizzing. A spent glow stick goes into the household bin intact. If one has split or leaked, nobody touches it: an adult bags it and bins it and any contact is rinsed for 15 minutes.
ALTERNATIVE (equal credit, no special equipment): Vary only surface area and concentration at room temperature - whole versus crushed tablet, full-strength versus diluted vinegar - eliminating all heating. Or analyse a published rate-versus-temperature dataset. Kitchen materials or paper.
ALWAYS - these rules hold in every lesson and nobody can switch them off:
  ALWAYS: Never mix household cleaning products; bleach combined with ammonia or acid releases toxic gas.
  ALWAYS: Never connect any investigation to mains electricity; low-voltage cells only.
  ALWAYS: Never fully seal a reacting, fermenting, oxidising, or warm mixture in any container.
  ALWAYS: Never have a flammable liquid open in the same room as a flame, hob, pilot light, heater, lamp, charger, or battery.
  ALWAYS: Never use alcohol, or any other fuel, for a flame demonstration; no open-flame demonstration is used anywhere in this package.
  ALWAYS: Never light, strike, or operate an open flame or a hob, burner, or pilot light for any investigation in this package; no lesson requires one.
  ALWAYS: Never cut, tear, puncture, or open a sealed commercial product - cold pack, hand warmer, glow stick, or smoke detector.
  ALWAYS: Never look at the sun directly or through any lens, filter, grating, or camera.
  ALWAYS: Never require a photograph, video, or voice recording as evidence of completion.
  ALWAYS: Never request or record a learner body measurement, health measurement, or medical history.
  ALWAYS: Never present invented measurements as real experimental results.

lesson_flow.title: Safety review before any material is handled
lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action:
READ THIS BEFORE YOU TOUCH ANY MATERIAL.
HAZARD (chemical): Acidic and basic solutions sting eyes and irritate skin.
MITIGATION: Wear eye protection, work over a tray, use small volumes with droppers, and rinse any splash with water for 15 minutes.
HAZARD (chemical): Household chemical mixing beyond the listed materials can produce toxic gas.
MITIGATION: Use ONLY cabbage indicator, vinegar, baking soda, and carbonated water. Never introduce a cleaning product. This prohibition is not disableable.
HAZARD (physical): A sealed carbonated bottle is a pressure vessel, and warming or shaking it turns the cap into a projectile.
MITIGATION: A carbonated bottle is never warmed above 40 degrees Celsius, never shaken while closed, and is always opened slowly with the cap pointed away from every face.
HAZARD (physical): Warm water can scald.
MITIGATION: An adult pours the warm bath and confirms with the thermometer that it reads below 50 degrees Celsius. Temperature is judged with the thermometer, never with a hand.
SUPERVISION: an adult must be beside you, watching, for the whole investigation. Do not start any step until they are there.

READ THIS BEFORE YOU TOUCH ANY MATERIAL.
HAZARD (physical): A domestic smoke detector contains a sealed radioactive source and is safe only while it stays intact.
MITIGATION: A smoke detector is never opened, dismantled, or taken apart, and its source is never removed or handled. A working smoke alarm is a safety device and stays installed and intact. This prohibition is not disableable.
HAZARD (physical): Large numbers of small counters spread and can be a choking hazard.
MITIGATION: Work in a shallow tray, keep counters away from young children, and count them back at the end.
HAZARD (emotional): Nuclear topics can raise anxiety about weapons or accidents.
MITIGATION: Content stays on decay physics, energy scale, and engineering trade-offs; the learner may pause or redirect to the materials strand at any point.
SUPERVISION: you may work on this independently. Tell an adult before you start anyway.
SAFE ORDER - do these steps in this order and do not reorder them:
  SAFE ORDER 1. Set the shallow tray down and move young children out of the work area before counters come out.
  SAFE ORDER 2. Count the 100 counters in and record the starting number.
  SAFE ORDER 3. Run each generation, removing and recording before the next throw.
  SAFE ORDER 4. Never open, dismantle, or take apart a smoke detector; it is discussed as a phenomenon and never handled as equipment.
  SAFE ORDER 5. Count every counter back in and confirm the total before leaving.
STOP CONDITIONS - stop at once if any of these happens:
  STOP: Pause if nuclear content becomes distressing and continue with the materials trade-off strand.
  STOP: Stop if anyone begins to open or dismantle a smoke detector.
  STOP: NO RADIOACTIVE SOURCE OF ANY KIND IS USED OR ACQUIRED IN THIS UNIT.
  STOP: Stop for any injury, burn, spill, fume, or allergic reaction and tell the supervising adult.
  STOP: Stop if a material, tool, or step is not the one this lesson specifies.
  STOP: Burn: cool it under running cool water for 20 minutes. Do not use ice, butter, or ointment.
  STOP: Splash in an eye: rinse with running water for 15 minutes, holding the eyelid open, before anything else.
  STOP: Fumes or a strong smell: leave the room, open a window from outside the room, and do not go back in to tidy up.
  STOP: Fire: do not use water. Get everyone out, close the door, and call the emergency number. Smother a very small contained flame with a metal pan lid or a fire blanket only if that is safe to do without reaching over it.
  STOP: If anyone may have swallowed a magnet, a battery, or any material from a lesson, treat it as an emergency and seek medical help at once. Do not wait for symptoms.
  STOP: A pause, break, or switch to the alternative activity is never treated as failure.
DISPOSAL: Counters go back into a labelled container stored out of reach of young children. No radioactive source is used or acquired at any point and no smoke detector is opened, so there is nothing hazardous to dispose of.
ALTERNATIVE (equal credit, no special equipment): Model half-life with a single die and tally marks on paper instead of 100 coins, then complete the trade-off analysis from published materials data. Paper only.
ALWAYS - these rules hold in every lesson and nobody can switch them off:
  ALWAYS: Never mix household cleaning products; bleach combined with ammonia or acid releases toxic gas.
  ALWAYS: Never connect any investigation to mains electricity; low-voltage cells only.
  ALWAYS: Never fully seal a reacting, fermenting, oxidising, or warm mixture in any container.
  ALWAYS: Never have a flammable liquid open in the same room as a flame, hob, pilot light, heater, lamp, charger, or battery.
  ALWAYS: Never use alcohol, or any other fuel, for a flame demonstration; no open-flame demonstration is used anywhere in this package.
  ALWAYS: Never light, strike, or operate an open flame or a hob, burner, or pilot light for any investigation in this package; no lesson requires one.
  ALWAYS: Never cut, tear, puncture, or open a sealed commercial product - cold pack, hand warmer, glow stick, or smoke detector.
  ALWAYS: Never look at the sun directly or through any lens, filter, grating, or camera.
  ALWAYS: Never require a photograph, video, or voice recording as evidence of completion.
  ALWAYS: Never request or record a learner body measurement, health measurement, or medical history.
  ALWAYS: Never present invented measurements as real experimental results.

Ask the learner to notice, predict, estimate, or question before any instruction. Record the prediction; it is not graded.

lesson_flow.title: Model or mini-lesson
lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action: The safety review in the first segment has already been read aloud with the guardian present; do not begin until it has. Then model the procedure for: Half-life modelling and a materials trade-off analysis, following the safe order exactly as written. Confirm which path the family is running - the investigation or its no-special-equipment alternative. Both meet the same target.

lesson_flow.title: Guided practice
lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action: Set up and run the first trial together, or the first step of the alternative, keeping to the safe order in the safety review. Establish how each measurement is taken, how uncertainty is recorded, and how a trial that goes wrong is written down rather than discarded.

lesson_flow.title: Independent application
lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action: Work through the safe order in the safety review, in order, without reordering it. Stop at once if any stop condition happens. Then run the remaining trials and record your own data. No expected value is supplied beforehand and no result is ever filled in for you. If the data is messy, write down what happened and why it may have happened. Finish with the disposal steps in the safety review before anything is packed away.

student_activity: The learner completes a new application of fusion independently and records both the result and the reasoning, evidence, process, or design choice that produced it.
